name: addpipe16_ripple3_sklansky13
rationale: Across many attempts, all full-width hand-built prefix networks (Kogge-Stone, Sklansky, Han-Carlson, Brent-Kung) underperformed the native '+' baseline, yet the externally-observed frontier point 'ripple2_prefix14' (2-bit ripple + 14-bit prefix) scored notably better (75.28 reward) than any full 16-bit prefix tree (best full-prefix Sklansky only reached 74.62), showing a short ripple prefix stage combined with a slightly narrower parallel-prefix tree can beat pure full-width prefix trees. This suggests the optimum ripple-prefix split is near but not at 0 ripple bits, and the exact split (2 vs 3 vs other) has not been swept. This candidate tries a 3-bit ripple prefix (bits 0-2) feeding a 13-bit Sklansky prefix tree (bits 3-15) with the ripple carry injected via the standard G|(P&Cin) group-carry formula. This is a genuinely new split point (not previously attempted by this agent) that may land closer to, or beyond, the ripple2_prefix14 frontier point and possibly approach the (16,) baseline, while remaining architecturally distinct from all 11 prior attempts.
